data.narrative:
ABL Bio is a public-stage biotech company (KOSDAQ-listed) founded by Sang Hoon Lee, with total capital raised exceeding $5B through IPO and licensing agreements. The relevant comp universe consists of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 7 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, New Limit, Recursion Pharmaceuticals, and Freenome.

Two standard valuation methods cannot be applied to this target. Peer-median comparison is not viable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables—while 7 same-sector private peers exist, none meet the threshold of three or more datapoints when filtered by identical stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples is precluded by the absence of disclosed revenue figures; the Biotech & Health sector median P/S stands at 6.2x across the three public comps, but without ABL Bio's revenue on file, the multiple cannot be applied.

This analysis reveals a fundamental constraint common to early and mid-stage biotech valuations: insufficient disclosure prevents triangulation via standard metrics. A defensible valuation range would require either revenue disclosure from the target, identification of private funding rounds with explicit per-share or post-money terms, or asset-based methods tied to pipeline stage and probability-adjusted cash flows. Current data supports none of these approaches. Key uncertainty centers on the composition and clinical progress of ABL Bio's pipeline relative to the peer set.
